'''Hélène Perrin''' (born 1972) is a French [[physicist]] working on [[Ultracold atom|quantum gas]] at Laser Physics Laboratory of [[Université Sorbonne Paris Nord]] and [[CNRS]], where she is a research director and leads the Bose-Einstein Condensate group.<ref>[http://www-lpl.univ-paris13.fr/bec/BEC/PosterTalk/2020_notice_Perrin_en.pdf  Helene Perrin CV – Sorbonne Paris Nord University]</ref><ref>[https://spie.org/OP/special-events/Plenary-Event?SSO=1 SPIE Optics+Photonics 2020 Plenary speakers]</ref>

She is head of the QuanTiP network, gathering all the actors on quantum technologies in Paris region.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Hélène Perrin, une physicienne au cœur de la révolution quantique {{!}} Région Île-de-France |url=https://www.iledefrance.fr/toutes-les-actualites/helene-perrin-une-physicienne-au-coeur-de-la-revolution-quantique |access-date=2026-03-31 |website=www.iledefrance.fr |language=fr}}</ref>

== Education and career ==
Hélène Perrin studied physics and engineering at the [[Ecole Polytechnique|École Polytechnique]] after studying at [[Lycée Louis-le-Grand]], and pursued a master's degree in quantum physics at [[Ecole Normale Superieure|École Normale Superieure]], before pursuing a PhD under the supervision of Christophe Salomon within [[Claude Cohen-Tannoudji]]'s group on the topic of [[ultracold atoms]],<ref>[https://tel.archives-ouvertes.fr/tel-00003896/en/  Refroidissement d'atomes de césium confinés dans un piège dipolaire très désaccordé]</ref>  which she completed in 1998. She then joined the [[French Alternative Energies and Atomic Energy Commission]] as a postdoctoral fellow before becoming a [[CNRS]] staff scientist in 1999.
